name: Y2K Design
visualIdentity: Supplemental reference for turn-of-the-millennium digital optimism: chrome typography, transparent plastic, rounded devices, early-web elements, and bright accents. The source does not claim this is a directly named collection style.
suitableUses: Explicitly suited to optimistic brand moments. Good-fit guidance also names product and editorial introductions, explanations, illustrated or abstract narratives, and cinematic sequences. Retro app launches and campaign microsites are suggested hybrid uses.
limitations: Keep material rules coherent and metallic highlights from overpowering the message. Chrome and plastic are not universal requirements for every element. Avoid decorative motion that distracts, obscures copy, or conflicts with a continuous-shot or loop requirement. Supplemental provenance limits claims about canonical style rules.
palette: Optional five-token suggestion for new artwork only: background #E9EDF0, foreground #293341, accents #7497D0, #DB8CBB, #A5C365. Preserve task, brand, reference, semantic-role, and asset colors; do not auto-adjust or expand approved palettes. Gradients are disabled. The foreground on accent 1 misses the 4.5 normal-text target (4.306); listed pairs on accents 2 and 3 pass the two-color check. Recheck actual compositing.
motionAndInteraction: Suggested style motions include rotations, elastic reveals, and interface assembly. Interactive HTML can use real buttons and tabs, focus states, responsive window stacking, and optional reduced-motion-aware press animations. Scroll-driven chapters or story steps are optional patterns, not style requirements; video must use deterministic composition time, with readable holds and reversible, seekable states.
audio: No fixed soundtrack is specified. Choose music, narration, vocals, effects, ambience, or silence for the topic and audience; honor supplied requirements and assets. Synchronize and mix with picture, preserving speech intelligibility and avoiding clipping or competing vocals.
assetRequirements: No specific assets are mandated. Use real DOM or SVG for interface elements and 3D materials for metallic type and plastic objects when needed. Load fonts and assets locally; seed randomness and cache stateful simulations. Distinguish simulated appearance from physical production.
combinations: Style 095 is suggested for functioning early-web UI in retro app launches: reserve chrome for one hero, use primary tokens, and avoid glassmorphism blur. Style 106 adds volume-preserving squash to plastic devices and buttons; keep one timing family, never squash text, and avoid applying uniform springs everywhere. Candidate motion patterns are optional and must fit the actual scene.
productionApproach: Select visual and motion tools by style, action, assets, and fidelity. Three.js builds 3D geometry/materials; HTML/CSS and SVG handle text and interfaces. Give each animated property one owner and expose deterministic state at composition time. HyperFrames is the primary assembly, timing, sync, validation, and export pipeline; use Remotion only if unavailable or a verified limitation blocks a requirement, recording the reason. Render checks and delivery instructions are specified in the source.
